object.definition: Reward laws $\nu_i(t)$ for the $K\ge2$ arms are fixed before interaction and evolve with absolute time, including for unpulled arms. Means satisfy $$\mu_i(t)=\mathbb E_{X\sim\nu_i(t)}X\in[0,1],\qquad \gamma_i(t)=\mu_i(t+1)-\mu_i(t)\ge0.$$. Decreasing increments are not required; there is no temporal concavity assumption. $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\max_{i\in[K]}\gamma_i(t)\le V,\qquad 0\le V\le K.$$

feedback_quality.noise: Each X_(i,t) has fixed mean mu_i(t), is sigma-sub-Gaussian, and is independent of the full reward-table history before t; within-time cross-arm dependence is irrelevant because one reward is selected.

operation.query_signature: Choose $I_t\in[K]$ from past observations and receive only $X_{I_t,t}$. Each $X_{i,t}$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian around $\mu_i(t)$ and independent of the reward table before round $t$; within-round dependence across arms is permitted. Only means, not realizations, must lie in $[0,1]$. Causal bandit policies are allowed. Inputs $K,T,\sigma,V$ are public and mean functions are hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

steps: Choose $I_t\in[K]$ using past observations, then observe only $X_{I_t,t}$. Rewards of other arms in the same round are hidden.

Each $X_{i,t}$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian around $\mu_i(t)$ and is independent of the entire reward table before round $t$. Within-round dependence across arms does not affect the single-arm feedback model.
Only reward means are restricted to $[0,1]$; realized rewards need not lie in that interval.
Causal bandit policies are allowed. Public inputs are $K,T,\sigma,V$.
The mean function is not revealed.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries.
